name: Tory
summary: Toryism is the British traditionalist strand of conservatism that grew out of the Cavalier royalists and the 17th-century party defending the Crown and the Church of England. It stands for monarchy, an established church, inherited institutions and a hierarchical but organic social order, and in its one-nation form holds that the governing classes owe responsibility to the poor and should reconcile the classes. It is cautious about reform, sceptical of abstract reason and doctrinaire markets or planning, and attached to nation and Empire.
scope: The British Tory tradition from the Stuart royalists through Burke, Disraeli's one-nation Toryism and the post-war paternalists, treated as traditionalist conservatism. It excludes the Canadian and American Tory usages and the free-market New Right. Many answers on modern issues are low-confidence inferences, since the sources document principles rather than programmes.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Later one-nation Conservatives accepted the post-war welfare state and the NHS.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: One-nation paternalism favours labour protection but nothing here addresses wage floors; adherents split.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Toryism is not doctrinaire about markets; they are accepted within custom, and Tories were split between protection and enterprise.

public-ownership.rationale: Post-war paternalists tolerated nationalised industry while others favoured enterprise; no settled Tory line.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Landed property and inheritance are valued, so higher wealth taxes are inferred to be disfavoured.

unions-good.rationale: Class cooperation favours accommodating labour, but Toryism is not a labour movement; inferred split.

property-fundamental.rationale: Burke tied liberties to landed property and conservatives value property as a support of social order.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Disraeli-era labour reforms show a willingness to regulate employers for the welfare of workers.

cut-welfare.rationale: Paternalism and the aim of reconciling the classes favour social provision over cutting it.

worker-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the defence of existing property and hierarchy rather than collective ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Conservatism stands on the side of authority and order, so security powers are inferred to be acceptable.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Traditional morality and order point against legalisation; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The tradition did not address this; adherents split between order and liberty.

strong-leader.rationale: Tories defend the Crown, Parliament and inherited institutions rather than leaders bypassing them.

state-harmful.rationale: Toryism values authority and established institutions; the state is a necessary organ of the social order.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; rural Tories and order-minded Tories diverge.

empower-police-military.rationale: Strong armed forces and order are described as hallmarks of later Toryism.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Inferred from the traditional moral order the tradition defends.

decide-locally.rationale: Local communities matter to the organic view, but Toryism also defends a central Crown and Parliament.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred split between order and paternalist reform.

traditional-family.rationale: Family, property and religion are the institutions in which the conservative organic society places its faith.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Inferred from traditionalism; modern Conservative leaders have split on it.

abortion-legal.rationale: Inferred from the religious and traditional orientation of High Toryism.

more-religion-public.rationale: Tories historically stood for high-church Anglicanism and the established church: God, King and Country.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Inferred from the preference for inherited arrangements over active social engineering.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from a traditionalism that treats natural order as a guide.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Tradition and patriotism are core conservative virtues, and the Tory motto names God, King and Country.

gradual-change.rationale: Burke's cautious, restorative reform is the model, and Tories opposed radical change.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Inferred from attachment to national tradition; the sources do not address immigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Tory loyalty is to Crown, nation and Empire, so supranational authority is inferred to be disfavoured.

free-trade.rationale: Documented split: most Tories backed Corn Law protection while Peelites embraced free trade.

nation-first.rationale: Patriotism is a fundamental conservative virtue; inferred for international cooperation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Not addressed; adherents split between interventionism and caution.

open-borders.rationale: Contrary to attachment to nation and inherited community; inferred.

limit-growth.rationale: Inferred; Tories value stewardship but not curbs on growth.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Anachronistic; Tories split between caution about change and drastic state action.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Scepticism about progress and the limits of reason point away from technological optimism.

revolution-justified.rationale: Burke and the Tories opposed the French Revolution and favoured only cautious reform.

experts-over-public.rationale: Burke favoured rule by the qualified yet distrusted abstract reason; inferred split.

central-planning.rationale: Conservatives reject doctrinaire planning as well as doctrinaire laissez-faire.

socialized-markets.rationale: Inferred from defence of existing property.

land-value-tax.rationale: Inferred from the value placed on landed property.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance sustains family and landed continuity; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: Inferred from paternalism that favours moral and social guidance over unconditional payments.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Tories were protectionist over agriculture in the Corn Law era but later accepted free trade.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Interventionism is a later Tory hallmark, but no stated view on strategic investment.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Property is valued but Tory thought favoured landed hierarchy; inferred split.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Wholly opposed to the order Toryism defends.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Inferred from rejection of radical monetary experiments.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Class cooperation is favoured but state-recognised bodies are not documented as Tory policy.

one-party-rule.rationale: Toryism evolved in a parliamentary party system under the Crown.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Tories are monarchists; God, King or Queen and Country is the tradition's motto.

democracy-best.rationale: Tory democracy accepted the franchise after 1867, while Burke doubted that a head-count expresses the people's will.

direct-votes.rationale: Burke questioned the head-count majority; representation by the qualified is preferred.

workers-councils.rationale: Inferred from the defence of inherited institutions.

right-to-secede.rationale: Tory loyalists opposed secession from the Crown and the Empire.

natural-rulers.rationale: High Tories defend hierarchy, natural order and aristocracy.

political-violence-never.rationale: Royalist tradition fought civil wars but later Toryism stressed order; adherents split.

war-builds-character.rationale: Inferred; the tradition values order and prudence over war as ennobling.

separate-church-state.rationale: Tories historically supported the established Church of England.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Support for an established church is not law by scripture; inferred as no.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Inferred from reverence for Crown and state institutions.

military-superiority.rationale: Strong armed forces and Empire imply support; inferred.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Tory loyalty was to Crown and Empire across peoples; inferred.

class-struggle-history.rationale: One-nation Toryism holds that classes should be reconciled, not set against each other.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Burke's order rests on inequality and hierarchy.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Inferred from imperial sovereignty and property emphasis.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's loyalty to Empire.

civilizational-union.rationale: Empire-Commonwealth ties mattered but no civilizational union is documented.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Noblesse oblige holds that the privileged owe duties, not mere self-interest.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Burke treats rights as inherited patrimony and society as a partnership across generations.

direct-action.rationale: Inferred from reverence for institutions and gradual change.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Inferred from the defence of settled social order.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Inferred; paternalist relief is not distribution by need as a principle.

production-for-use.rationale: Inferred from acceptance of markets and property.

profit-exploitation.rationale: Inferred from defence of property and class cooperation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Contrary to the order Toryism defends.

collective-farming.rationale: Contrary to the defence of landed property.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Inferred from the tradition's acceptance of property and Empire.

taxation-theft.rationale: Conservatives treat the state as a necessary authority.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Later Conservative policy but not a Tory principle.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: One-nation figures and the New Right split.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Inferred; Disraeli blamed institutions and the neglect of the poor.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: The sources do not address this; Tories are indifferent or split, so neutral is inferred.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; paternalism and markets pull both ways.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Toryism accepts state coercion, war and armed forces in defence of order; inferred.

party-commands-army.rationale: The armed forces owe loyalty to the Crown.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: The sources do not address this; Tories are indifferent or split, so neutral is inferred.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: The sources do not address this; Tories are indifferent or split, so neutral is inferred.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Tories historically held that office should go to those with property and standing, and Disraeli's world paid MPs nothing; inferred, and hostile to a pay cap that would exclude them.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Burkean Toryism holds that representatives owe their judgment, not obedience, to anyone, though modern Conservative parties use whips; inferred.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Toryism is attached to nation, Crown and parliamentary sovereignty, and modern Tories lean Eurosceptic, though some one-nation Conservatives backed European union.

head-commands-forces.rationale: High Tories defend the Crown's prerogative, but the settled British Tory view accepts ministers answerable to Parliament, so support is moderate.

church-by-bishops.rationale: The Tory party arose to defend the Church of England and its episcopal order against dissent and congregational Puritanism.

clerical-rule.rationale: Tories defend an established church alongside the Crown and Parliament, not rule by clergy.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Toryism is bound to nation, Crown and Empire, and treats wartime disloyalty as treason.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Tory traditionalism values moral order and religion, and Tory governments upheld censorship, but the sources do not address art directly; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Tory tradition is about parliamentary government with no fixed limits on prime ministers, and has little to say on presidents; inferred.

recall-officials.rationale: Burke's Tory view is that representatives exercise independent judgment and are judged at elections, which is incompatible with recall.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Tories were attached to nation and Empire and to a strong military, so ending alliances and withdrawing troops is not their line; inferred.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: The Tory tradition defends property and the landed order, so abolishing renting in favour of universal owner-occupation is contrary to it; inferred.

people-in-arms.rationale: Tories prized a professional army and the Crown's command of it, so an armed citizenry is unlikely; inferred.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: The Tory tradition grew from the landed gentry and country interest and often idealises rural life; inferred.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: The sources do not address reunifying divided nations and Tory attitudes are mixed; inferred.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: Burkean scepticism of abstract reason makes Tories wary of theorists and intellectuals cut off from practical life; inferred.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Tories treat civilisations as shaped by inherited institutions and often prize the British tradition above others; inferred.

death-penalty.rationale: Traditional Tories supported capital punishment, though the sources do not discuss terrorism; inferred.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: One-nation Tories accepted social reform, but traditionalists doubted progressive school curricula and adherents are split; inferred.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The strand is tied to the established Church of England, whose teaching accepts evolution, so creationism in schools is not a Tory cause; inferred.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Traditionalist conservatism defends public morals and favours legal limits on obscenity; inferred.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: A tradition based on lineage, Crown and inherited institutions fits descent-based membership of the nation; inferred.

minority-language-support.rationale: One-nation Toryism stresses reconciling classes and regions, but the sources do not address minority-language support.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Tories defended the established church and general law over claims of exemption for dissenting groups; inferred.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Burke's defence of custom and prescription favours conformity to inherited ways over encouraging eccentricity; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Tories defend inherited rights and obligations and distrust abrupt redistributive measures; inferred from the respect for property and prescription in the conservatism entry.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Tories valued Empire and inherited constitutional order over transforming the economic system; inferred, since the sources do not address decolonisation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Burkean Toryism opposes remaking a constitution from scratch by assembly, preferring inherited institutions and gradual reform.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Tories favour order and authority, but paternalism and the rule of law sit badly with sacrificing freedoms for growth; inferred.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: One-nation noblesse oblige is directed at the poor of one nation and Empire; whether it extends to aid abroad is not addressed and adherents split.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Attachment to nation and national sovereignty suggests support for an independent deterrent; inferred, as the sources predate nuclear weapons.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Toryism is monarchist and defends an inherited head of state against election.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Not addressed by Tory sources; paternalists favoured active government while others valued sound money, so adherents split.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Not addressed by the Tory sources; inference from national attachment is offset by pragmatic caution, so adherents split.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Burkean and one-nation Toryism treat property as carrying duties to those beneath, with the governing classes owing responsibility to the poor.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Tories would reject the label of socialism for the USSR and condemn it as collectivist tyranny; the state-capitalist reading is not theirs, so inferred.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Burkean caution and stewardship of inherited things favour protective action; inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Tories prize the nation and alliances that protect Crown and Empire, and post-war Conservatives backed NATO; inferred.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Toryism defended an empire acquired partly by conquest but also prized law and prescription; adherents are split.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Tories defend the established Church of England and its endowments against civil encroachment.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: Tories defend the Crown as a symbol of national continuity standing above party.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Tories are Unionists who defend the integrity of the United Kingdom; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Toryism values inherited institutions, and Scots law and local customs sit within the British Union; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Early Tories held divine right, but later Toryism dropped it and treats the monarchy as an historic office; inferred.

flat-income-tax.rationale: One-nation Toryism accepts that the better off should bear a larger share, so a flat tax is disfavoured; inferred.

character-from-environment.rationale: Conservatism holds that human nature is imperfect and largely fixed, so people cannot be remade by circumstance; inferred.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Tories prize ancient law and the constitution, and Burke held rulers bound by the laws and customs of the realm.

space-expansion.rationale: Space expansion is anachronistic for Toryism; adherents are split.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The mixed British constitution of Crown, Lords and Commons is the classic Tory ideal.

leader-cult.rationale: Tories reverence the Crown and institutions rather than individual leaders, and distrust public adulation; inferred.

equal-parenting.rationale: Toryism does not address custody law; adherents are split.

missingStatements.text: Those with wealth and rank owe obligations to the poor beneath them.
missingStatements.rationale: Noblesse oblige is the defining ethic of one-nation Toryism, and Disraeli's Sybil is written to expose neglect of the people.

missingStatements.text: A hereditary aristocracy should keep a role in governing the country.
missingStatements.rationale: High Tories defend hierarchy, natural order and aristocracy.

notes: High Tories and one-nation paternalists would diverge from the free-market Thatcherite wing, which is excluded here; modern Conservative Party members vary widely on social issues.
